::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 3. 1865  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS. 55384 (2): P. 625
:::

My dear Miss Yonge	
Your scheme as decided by [Miss Sewell](people/person_1301.qmd) and yourself seems to me very admirable.[^1] The one question is the compactness and vivid unity, which will be hard rather in an [*illegible*] such as you propose. But with artists like yourself [and] Miss Sewell there should be no difficulty[.] the thing ought to be very interesting indeed.

[I](people/person_939.qmd)have read all the [Prince and the Page](cmy_books/cmybook_61.qmd) down to the present month. I think it delightful, and hope it will make a very nice Christmas book. But I confess I do not feel quite clear about the [illustration](organizations/other_167.qmd).[^2] At a first glance it does not quite please me. The Architecture in any case should be more subordinated, but my first impression of the figures is rather that they are weak. I will write more about it tomorrow.

ever most truly yours
A. Macmillan

The enclosed cheque is for both your [story](cmy_books/cmybook_62.qmd) & [paper](cmy_books/cmybook_59.qmd) - which [*illegible*] capital.

---

[^1]: The scheme was for the book which became *Historical Selections*.
[^2]: CMY was trying to persuade him to use a drawing by [Katie Johns](people/person_887.qmd).
